veranderings.rede: In written narrative 'gevind' is the standard word for 'found'; 'gekry' is colloquial here.
The separable compound verb 'volpomp' is written as one word in the past participle (volgepomp), as with volmaak and volgooi.

veranderings.voor: langs haar oor gehou sonder om iets te hoor
veranderings.na: langs haar oor gehou, maar sy het niks gehoor nie
veranderings.rede: 'Sonder om iets te hoor' reads like a literal translation of 'without hearing anything'; a clause with 'maar ... niks ... nie' is more natural, with the AWS comma because it has its own subject and verb.
'In ... ingedruk' says 'in' twice; the plain verb reads more cleanly.

veranderings.voor: op haar hurke gesit en Vusi
veranderings.na: op haar hurke gesit, en Vusi
veranderings.rede: AWS 2017: a comma before 'en' when it joins two clauses that each have their own subject and verb.
'Deur haar kop maal' is the idiomatic Afrikaans expression for words that keep going round in one's mind.
'Voordat' is the clearer conjunction in written text; 'voor' can also read as a preposition.

veranderings.voor: het sy gesê en weer geloop
veranderings.na: het sy gesê en weer weggestap
veranderings.rede: 'Weer geloop' can read as 'walked again'; 'weer weggestap' clearly means she left.
One runs one's fingers 'oor' a surface, matching 'haar vinger oor die rubber laat loop' earlier; 'aan' is unidiomatic with 'laat loop'.

veranderings.voor: Sy het gekyk dat die buiteband
veranderings.na: Sy het seker gemaak dat die buiteband
veranderings.rede: 'Gekyk dat' copies English 'checked that'; 'seker gemaak dat' is the natural Afrikaans and keeps the meaning.

beskerm_bedenkings.woord: Sy het die band droog gevee
beskerm_bedenkings.rede: Possible spelling point only: adjective plus verb units such as droogmaak are often written as one word (drooggevee); I am not certain the AWS requires it for 'droogvee', so it is left untouched and raised for a person. The unprotected 'die band weer droog gevee' later in the story is left as is so the two stay consistent.
